title: kt Rolster Defeats T1 and Hanwha Life Esports in Succession
summary: kt Rolster Defeats T1 and Hanwha Life Esports in Succession  Inven Global
content:
kt Rolster has joined the race for the top spot in the Legend Group after defeating both Hanwha Life Esports and T1—the first and second-place teams from the first two rounds of the regular season—to finish the first week of Round 3 with two consecutive wins. Dplus KIA, the EWC champions, also continued their momentum from the international stage by winning both of their matches in the first week of Round 3. In the Rise Group, Nongshim RedForce was the only team to record an undefeated week.

Riot Games, the organizer of the League of Legends Champions Korea (LCK)—the Korean professional league for League of Legends (LoL)—announced that the first week of the 2026 LCK regular season Round 3, held from Wednesday, July 29, to Sunday, August 2, at LoL PARK in Jongno-gu, Seoul, and Hall 5 of KINTEX Exhibition Center 1 in Goyang, Gyeonggi-do, has concluded.

kt Rolster secured a 2-0 sweep against T1 in the 'Telecommunications Derby' on July 29 (Wed) and followed up with a 2-1 victory over Hanwha Life Esports after a hard-fought full set on August 2 (Sun).

In the final match of the first week of Round 3, kt Rolster and Hanwha Life Esports traded dominant victories. After kt Rolster took the first set with a kill score of 36-12, Hanwha Life Esports struck back to win the second set 19-7. In the tense third set, kt Rolster secured the win after catching Hanwha Life Esports jungler 'Kanavi' Seo Jin-hyeok near the Baron pit, with bottom laner 'Fenrir' Park Gang-jun delivering a standout performance to close out the intense series.

Having defeated the top two teams from the first two rounds, kt Rolster now sits at 15-5, tied with Hanwha Life Esports and T1. While their rankings are currently separated by set differential, the three-way tie at 15-5 signals an increasingly fierce battle for the top of the Legend Group.

Dplus KIA, fresh off their victory at the Esports World Cup (EWC), defeated MSI champions Hanwha Life Esports and then took down Gen.G at the '2026 LCK Team Roadshow: Gen.G Homestand - House of Gen.G,' winning both of their matches in the first week of Round 3.
